note.question: How should a multinational combine audits with workforce retention or cross-training to reduce a supplier’s strategic use of excessive overtime without making compliance incentives backfire?
note.overview: A manufacturer commits to auditing and supplier-development instruments; after private workforce and public demand realize, the supplier strategically chooses whether to meet orders by forcing excessive overtime. The paper solves this sequential dyadic supply-chain game by backward induction.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In the auditing-only model, the manufacturer publicly chooses e∈{0,e_H} before demand and workforce realize. In the supplier-development extensions, it first makes a binary retention-subsidy decision y or binary cross-training decision z at the beginning of the horizon and then chooses the binary audit action. Demand and product-specific workforce realize; the manufacturer orders realized demand; the supplier privately observes workforce and selects production; internal and possibly external audits determine detection, penalties and goodwill losses. The supplier gains fulfillment margin from overtime but risks penalties and goodwill losses.
